definition: Humanistic psychology, in this packet, is a view of human life that puts human needs and values at the center of psychology. It emphasizes empathy, creativity, freedom, justice, and love, and treats alienation, control, aggressiveness, idolization, and emotional numbness as forces that can undermine peace and human flourishing.

reasons: The packet supports Fromm’s humanistic peace psychology, but not the broader definition of humanistic psychology as a general view of human life centered on human needs and values.
“Human flourishing” is not stated in the packet; the source speaks instead about peace, positive peace, and the psychological foundation for peace.
The field is not well supported as ethics; the packet situates the term in psychology/peace psychology rather than ethics.
The packet does not explicitly support the claim that humanistic psychology “puts human needs and values at the center of psychology.”

The packet does not explicitly support the phrasing that alienation/control/aggressiveness/etc. “undermine peace and human flourishing”; it discusses erosion of the psychological foundation for peace, but not “human flourishing.”

Some emphasized elements in the definition (e.g., “treats … as forces that can undermine peace”) are only partially supported: the packet ties aggressiveness/idolization/emotional numbness to war and discusses alienation/control in relation to “humanized technology,” but it does not state this broader ‘forces that can undermine’ framing for all listed items in the general terms used in the definition.
